brief: The canvas displays deep-sea hydrothermal mineral formations, depicting crystalline structures and complex lattices. The color palette shifts continually, simulating the mineral deposition process. The central movement is one of constant, relentless erosion and gradual crystal deposition, causing the existing material to fracture and reform in perpetuity. There is no external interaction required; the entire system evolves autonomously, modeling the continuous chemical action of the deep ocean floor.

statement: This sketch models the dynamic geological processes of deep-sea hydrothermal vents through an evolving particle system. The visualization depicts mineral formations as particles that undergo continuous erosion and deposition—particles drift chaotically due to noise-based forces, occasionally aggregating to form crystalline structures. The color palette shifts gradually over time, simulating the chemical changes during mineral precipitation. Connections between nearby particles form a lattice-like structure that constantly evolves as particles move and age, creating an ever-changing pattern reminiscent of natural crystal growth and fracture processes in oceanic environments.
